question.text: The length of the chord $x+y=3$ intercepted by the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-2 x-2 y-2=0$ is

solution.text: The centre of the circle is \(\mathrm{C}(1,1)\) and radius of the circle is 2 , perpendicular distance from \(\mathrm{C}\) on \(\mathrm{AB}\), the chord \(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=3\) \(\begin{aligned} &\mathrm{CD}=\left|\frac{1+1-3}{\sqrt{2}}\right|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ &\Rightarrow \mathrm{AD}=\sqrt{4-\frac{1}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{2}}\left[\mathrm{AD}=\sqrt{\mathrm{AC}^{2}-\mathrm{CD}^{2}}\right] \end{aligned}\) Hence, the length of the chord \(\mathrm{AB}=2 \mathrm{AD}=2 \sqrt{\frac{7}{2}}=\sqrt{14}\).
